note: Lightning Scheduler schedules future Content Moderation state transitions. It adds two revisionable base fields (scheduled_transition_date, scheduled_transition_state) to every moderated entity type, swaps the moderation_state widget for ModerationStateWidget, and runs due transitions on cron via TransitionManager. Its only editable config object is lightning_scheduler.settings with two keys: time_step (the time input's step in seconds: 1/60/300/600/900/1800/3600, default 60) and allow_past_dates (bool, default true). Permission 'administer lightning scheduler' gates the settings form; dynamic 'schedule <workflow> transition <transition>' permissions are derived from workflow transitions. Medium/hard cases are grounded in the two real config keys (this site currently has no moderated bundle, so no scheduling fields exist; config is the module's live surface).

evals.prompt: What does the Lightning Scheduler module do in Drupal, and what makes a scheduled moderation-state change actually happen at the scheduled time?
evals.expected_output: It lets editors schedule future Content Moderation state transitions on moderated entities (stored in the scheduled_transition_date / scheduled_transition_state base fields). On cron, TransitionManager processes due transitions and, if the workflow allows the from->to transition, sets moderation_state and saves.

evals.prompt: Which configuration options does Lightning Scheduler expose on its settings form, and in which config object are they stored?
evals.expected_output: Two options in the lightning_scheduler.settings config object: time_step (the scheduling time input's step in seconds) and allow_past_dates (whether past dates may be scheduled). Form at /admin/config/system/lightning/scheduler.

evals.prompt: What permissions does Lightning Scheduler add in Drupal, and how are the per-transition scheduling permissions named?
evals.expected_output: It adds 'administer lightning scheduler' (gates the settings form) plus a dynamic permission per workflow transition named like 'schedule <workflow> transition <transition>' (derived from Content Moderation's 'use <workflow> transition <transition>').

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, inspect the live Lightning Scheduler configuration and tell me the current value of its time input step (time_step), in seconds.
On this Drupal site, inspect the live Lightning Scheduler configuration and tell me whether authors are currently allowed to schedule transitions for dates in the past (the allow_past_dates setting).
evals.expected_output: No — allow_past_dates is false in lightning_scheduler.settings, so past-dated transitions are rejected.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure Lightning Scheduler so the scheduling time input steps in 5-minute increments (time_step = 300 seconds). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set lightning_scheduler.settings time_step to 300 (e.g. drush cset lightning_scheduler.settings time_step 300, or via the settings form).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure Lightning Scheduler so that authors cannot schedule transitions in the past AND the time input steps in 1-hour increments (time_step = 3600 seconds). Apply both changes to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set lightning_scheduler.settings allow_past_dates to false and time_step to 3600.
